text: An NFL star just made this tackle and didn't get up. Here's why they strapped him to a board.
Jack Campbell is an All Pro linebacker for the Detroit Lions.
Sunday at Ford Field the Lions led twelve to seven in the fourth quarter.
Vikings tight end TJ Hockenson caught a short pass over the middle.
Campbell and Eric O'Neill twisted him down at the twenty five.
Then Campbell stayed face down and didn't move.
Here's why that's so scary. The bones in your neck wrap around your spinal cord.
That cord carries the signals between your brain and your body.
A hard hit can bend the neck too far and pinch the cord. Then the arms and legs can stop working.
So trainers hold his head still and strap him to a hard board so his neck can't move.
Players from both teams took a knee. About ten minutes later he was carted off.
He left alert and breathing. The Lions won nineteen to fifteen.
Wednesday he said he has full movement in his lower body and his upper body is getting better.
